title: Part Two: What We Actually Have: The Electoral College

sections.brief: How the EC is built: 538/270, two-senator floor, DC's three (CRS 2026); Article II leaves method to legislatures; 1800 tie and 12th Amendment (distinct ballots, House one vote per state, 1824 contingent election); winner-take-all spread for partisan reasons (Virginia 1800, Jefferson, by 1836 all but SC, Colorado 1876); Maine 1972 and Nebraska 1992 district method, splits to 2024; ECRA counting steps; worked example of an Omaha ballot in 2024; Biden 2020 margin on <50,000 votes; 2024 49.8% to 312 EV; constitutional vs statutory parts. Figures: time, flow

Design claim vs outcome judgment: Federalist 68 quotes (12 Mar 1788); screen is an elite, not democratic, check; pledges since 1796, 12th Amendment 'made party-line voting safe', ~0.5% of EVs ever faithless; 2016 Hamilton Electors (KNKX), seven faithless votes (five Clinton, two Trump), $1,000 fines; Chiafalo 6 July 2020 9-0 (Thomas concurring in judgment), 32+DC pledge laws and 15 sanctions in 2020; 'not free agents'; both readings of 'failed in 2016' with measures (EIU 2016 caveat, FH from 94 in 2010, V-Dem 2025, Pew partisan flip). Figures: flow, compare

Five splits with margins (Britannica; CRS counts four), 2024 result; campaign concentration 2020/2024 (FairVote/NPV, flagged as advocates); fixes with route and status Oct 2026: Bayh-Celler 1969-70 (339-70; cloture 54-36, 53-34), recent amendments stalled (CRS); NPVIC 222 EV after Virginia 13 Apr 2026, critics (Valencia) and supporters; ECRA 2022 provisions and votes; Gallup 2020/2024 and Pew 2024 opinion with partisan movement; The test, incl. where record cuts against the thesis. Figures: compare (splits), stats (events), flow (NPVIC), compare (reforms)
